feed.title: Polar Star Project: alerts from the records

entry.title: ICE has not posted its required detention statistics
entry.summary: ICE's last detention statistics file is dated July 20, 2026: 84 days with no new file when ICE's page was checked on October 12, 2026. Congress asked for this file every two weeks, so about 6 updates have been missed. The requirement was added in the fiscal 2020 DHS appropriations law; reporting has noted debate over whether it still binds ICE.

entry.title: Share of people in ICE detention held more than a year
entry.summary: 4,161 people in ICE detention on August 6, 2026 had been held more than a year, and 12,736 more than six months (6.3% and 19.3% of the 65,890 held). Long stays often come from cases still before a judge or on appeal, which can take more than a year. ICE's records do not say why any one stay has lasted this long, whether it has been reviewed, or whether the person has a final removal order. ICE's own twice-monthly file gives a lower figure, 2,112 held more than a year on June 30, 2026. This count runs from the start of each continuous stay in ICE detention, across transfers; ICE's file does not say how it measures, so the two are not directly comparable. For people with a final removal order, the Supreme Court set six months as the presumptively reasonable limit when removal is not reasonably foreseeable (Zadvydas v. Davis, 2001). The records cannot show how many of these stays that applies to; that is the question for the bodies below.

entry.title: Adams County Correctional Center: share held more than a year well above other facilities
entry.summary: 422 of the 2,415 people held here on August 6, 2026 had been in ICE detention more than a year (17%), against 6.3% of everyone held. At the national share, a count this high would come up by chance less than once in 100. Long stays often come from cases still in court or on appeal; the records do not say which.

entry.title: Adelanto ICE Processing Center: deaths well above other facilities
entry.summary: 4 deaths ICE reported here from August 2025 to July 2026: 24.4 for every 10,000 people held for a year, against 6.2 across all facilities on ICE's list over the same months. At the overall rate, a count this high would come up by chance about 2 times in 100. Officials were refused entry here 1 time since August 2025. This is listed beside the figures above as a fact; it does not show that one caused the other. About 1,635 people a day were held here from August 2025 to July 2026. Rates from a handful of deaths move a lot with one event.
